## 8. ANN genomic predictions

The published analysis uses the previously fitted ANN outputs rather than
running the networks again. The four saved objects provide model-level
performance (`results`), individual held-out predictions (`predictions`),
epoch-selection diagnostics (`epoch_selection`), and execution metadata
(`final_meta`). Reading these files preserves the evaluated outer splits and
keeps result presentation separate from model fitting.

```{r saved-final-results}
# Read the stored model metrics, predictions and epoch-selection results.
results <- readRDS(FINAL_RESULTS_RDS)
predictions <- readRDS(FINAL_PREDICTIONS_RDS)
epoch_selection <- readRDS(FINAL_EPOCH_RDS)
final_meta <- readRDS(FINAL_RUN_RDS)

```

The reader uses the canonical final-result RDS files and their stored run
metadata. Their configuration identifiers, content schemas and file digests
should be checked in a separate read-only audit before publication; the
workflowr status alone does not establish the integrity of these scientific
artifacts. No administrative runtime assertions are embedded here.

```{r final-records-summary}
# Summarize the saved outputs and their unique outer task counts.
final_output_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "Model-task results",
    "Held-out predictions",
    "Epoch selections"
  ),
  Rows = c(
    nrow(results),
    nrow(predictions),
    nrow(epoch_selection)
  ),
  Unique_tasks = c(
    length(unique(results$TaskID)),
    length(unique(predictions$TaskID)),
    length(unique(epoch_selection$TaskID))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


final_output_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Stored final ANN result structure",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The stored benchmark contains **600 model-task results**, **120,000 held-out
predictions**, and **600 epoch-selection records**. The historical `Status =
"ok"` field indicates that a fit returned and produced stored predictions; it is
not interpreted as a formal proof of numerical convergence.

## 9. Predictive performance

Recovery of the known true genetic value is the primary evaluation target.
Phenotype prediction is retained as a secondary target because phenotype also
contains residual variation.

### 9.1 Evaluation metrics

For held-out individual $i$, let $t_i$ denote the evaluation target (true
genetic value or observed phenotype), let $\hat y_i$ denote the ANN
prediction and let $n$ be the number of held-out individuals. The original
scale is preserved for all metrics:

\[
\mathrm{RMSE}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat y_i-t_i)^2},
\qquad
\mathrm{MAE}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\hat y_i-t_i|,
\qquad
\mathrm{Bias}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat y_i-t_i).
\]

Pearson correlation measures linear association between $\hat y$ and $t$;
Spearman correlation measures the association of their ranks. The calibration
slope is the coefficient of $\hat y$ in the regression
$t=\alpha+\beta\hat y+\varepsilon$; it is therefore
target-on-prediction, not the reverse.
The metric calculations are identical for both targets.

### 9.2 Predictive performance by scenario

The next table averages the stored held-out genetic-value metrics over the 25
outer splits for each scenario and ANN variant. The scenario's QTL count and
nominal heritability remain descriptive columns; the averaged results describe
the observed cross-validation performance rather than independent experiments.

```{r performance-summary}
# Average held-out performance over outer splits by scenario and ANN model.
ok <- results[
  results$Status == "ok",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

scenario_performance <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Genetic_Pearson,
    Genetic_Spearman,
    Genetic_RMSE,
    Genetic_MAE,
    Genetic_Bias,
    Genetic_Slope,
    Phenotype_Pearson,
    Phenotype_Spearman,
    Phenotype_RMSE,
    Phenotype_MAE,
    Phenotype_Bias,
    Phenotype_Slope
  ) ~ Scenario + Model + QTL_N + H2_nominal,
  data = ok,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

scenario_performance <- scenario_performance[
  order(
    match(scenario_performance$Scenario, scenario_names),
    match(scenario_performance$Model, MODEL_LEVELS)
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


scenario_performance[
  , c(
    "Scenario",
    "Model",
    "QTL_N",
    "H2_nominal",
    "Genetic_Pearson",
    "Genetic_Spearman",
    "Genetic_RMSE",
    "Genetic_MAE",
    "Genetic_Bias",
    "Genetic_Slope"
  )
] |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Primary evaluation: mean outer-split ANN performance against true genetic value",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Here, larger **Pearson correlation** means stronger linear association with the
known genetic signal. Smaller RMSE and MAE indicate smaller absolute prediction
error. Bias near zero and calibration slope near one describe calibration on the
held-out scale.

```{r phenotype-performance}
# Present the phenotype-based metrics separately from genetic-value recovery.
scenario_performance[
  , c(
    "Scenario",
    "Model",
    "Phenotype_Pearson",
    "Phenotype_Spearman",
    "Phenotype_RMSE",
    "Phenotype_MAE",
    "Phenotype_Bias",
    "Phenotype_Slope"
  )
] |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Secondary evaluation: mean outer-split ANN performance against phenotype",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

### 9.3 Held-out performance across outer splits

The next figures display all 25 outer-split results for each scenario and ANN
variant. Their purpose is descriptive: repeated outer folds overlap in the
individuals used for model fitting, so the 25 values are **not treated as 25
statistically independent replicates or as inferential uncertainty**.

```{r genetic-correlation-figure, fig.cap="Held-out true genetic-value Pearson correlation for the four ANN variants across the 25 outer splits in each scenario. White diamonds indicate model means within scenario."}
# Visualize split-level Pearson correlations descriptively.
p_ann_correlation <- ggplot(
  ok,
  aes(
    x = Model,
    y = Genetic_Pearson,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.62,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.70
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.10,
      height = 0,
      seed = SEED_GLOBAL + 401L
    ),
    alpha = 0.35,
    size = 1.4
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 2.8,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_gdocs() +
  labs(
    x = "ANN variant",
    y = "Pearson correlation with true genetic value",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 35,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

print(p_ann_correlation)
```

### 9.4 Overall ANN comparison

To complement the scenario-specific results, this table averages each
held-out genetic-value metric across the 150 outer tasks for each ANN variant.
It reports Pearson and Spearman correlations alongside RMSE and MAE. Because
the six scenarios differ in their simulated genetic settings, these pooled
means are descriptive: scenario-level comparisons remain necessary, and the
summary alone does not establish statistical significance between models.

```{r overall-ann-summary}
# Pool scenario-specific held-out genetic-value metrics by ANN variant.
overall_ann <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Genetic_Pearson,
    Genetic_Spearman,
    Genetic_RMSE,
    Genetic_MAE
  ) ~ Model,
  data = ok,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

overall_ann <- overall_ann[
  match(MODEL_LEVELS, overall_ann$Model),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


overall_ann |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Overall ANN performance against true genetic value",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Across all outer tasks, the four ANN variants are summarized descriptively
with the common held-out predictive metrics. Interpretation of regularization
effects and the complete task-matched comparison with GBLUP-A, GBLUP-AD, and
GBLUP-ADE are reserved for M05.
